justifications.type_expressiveness: Good use of enums for Expr/Value/UnaryOp/BinaryOp/EvalError, but TypeError variant carries a free-form String instead of structured operand/operator info, and ParseError likewise uses a String message.
justifications.error_handling: Typed EvalError enum with the three required variants, no panics in library code, but several unreachable!() calls are undocumented and ParseError relies on stringly-typed messages.
justifications.api_ergonomics: Sensible derives and Display impls exist, but no doc comments appear on any public item, and ParseError exposes raw public fields rather than accessor methods.
justifications.idiomaticity: Generally idiomatic Rust with ?, matches!, and a clean recursive-descent parser, though the linked-list Env and repeated boilerplate match arms are mildly non-idiomatic and a few clones could be avoided.
